title: Value a warehouse's stock on every core

blocks.text: The warehouse team needs the value of its stock: for every SKU, the quantity on hand times the unit price, summed, plus the number of SKUs that are out of stock. A big warehouse has a few million SKUs, and each price is a lookup in the price list, so the valuation runs on a `ForkJoinPool`. One `StockValuation` is created at startup and shared: the nightly report uses it, and so does the "value now" button on the warehouse screen, which people press at any time, including while the nightly report is running.
Finish `Totals.plus` and `compute()` of the `Value` task in `src/main/java/practice/StockValuation.java`. When you're done:

items: every valuation returns the value and the out-of-stock count of the SKUs it was given, including for an empty warehouse and for values far beyond 21 million euros;
a valuation gives the same totals the second time it is asked, and while another one runs.

blocks.text: About fifteen lines in total. The tests run real pools of two and three workers.

cases.says: a new StockValuation values the stock and counts the SKUs out of stock, for empty, small and large warehouses, any threshold, and values beyond the int range
a second valuation on the same StockValuation starts from nothing, rather than from the first one's totals
two valuations running at once on the same StockValuation each return the totals of their own SKUs

origin.section: A Task Returns Its Part of the Answer; Tasks That Write into Shared State Lose It

concepts: Each task returns its part of the answer and the parent combines the values it joins; leaves that write into shared state lose updates, and a thread-safe field held by the object that runs the task still mixes the totals of two runs.
